steps.say: Most navel bulges in toddlers vanish on their own, so reassurance starts the visit. About 80 percent of umbilical hernias close spontaneously, and elective repair waits until around 5 years of age. Measuring the ring at each visit is tracking the natural narrowing.
steps.tx: About **80** percent of **umbilical hernia** (navel bulges) close by **spontaneous closure** (natural ring narrowing), so elective repair waits until around **5** years in the **timing of repair** (planned age for surgery). Serial ring measurement tracks progress at clinic visits.

vis.alt: Paediatric abdominal regions chart beside inspection panels showing scaphoid abdomen, umbilical hernia bulge and visible gastric peristalsis.
vis.caption: Most navel bulges narrow as the rectus matures; measure the ring at each visit. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Parents often fear trapping of bowel, yet this complication is vanishingly rare at the navel. Incarceration is extremely rare, separating umbilical hernias from inguinal hernias in urgency. Risk stratification keeps most children safely on observation while inguinal hernias hurry to theatre.
steps.tx: **Incarceration** (trapped bowel) is extremely rare, separating umbilical hernias from **inguinal hernia** (groin rupture needing early surgery) in urgency. **Risk stratification** (sorting by danger) keeps navel hernias on observation while groin hernias are listed promptly. Groin lumps with vomiting or a tender testis need same day review.

steps.say: A widening bulge or a broad ring brings the operation forward from the fifth birthday. Earlier repair is considered when the enlarging hernia grows over time or the fascial defect exceeds 2 centimetres. Documenting the ring size at every visit is supporting that decision with numbers.
steps.tx: Earlier repair is considered when the **enlarging hernia** (growing bulge) progresses over time or the **fascial defect** (ring gap) exceeds **2** cm, creating a **surgical indication** (reason to operate early). Annual measurement with a tape keeps the threshold objective. Photograph the defect at each visit for comparison over time.

vis.alt: Sagittal abdominal wall anatomy with paediatric hernia bulge and closure pathway beside adult repair with suture and mesh options.
vis.caption: Repair moves earlier when the bulge enlarges or the fascial defect exceeds 2 centimetres. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: A trunk like flap of leftover skin after late closure looks poor and upsets families. A skin proboscis over 3 centimetres after neglected closure gives poor cosmesis, which also argues for timely repair. Operating before the skin stretches is preserving the navel shape.
steps.tx: A skin **proboscis** (trunk like flap) over **3** cm after neglected closure gives poor **cosmesis** (navel appearance), which also argues for timely repair. **Skin excess** (redundant stretched skin) is avoided by operating before years of stretching deform the ring. Late referrals need counselling about likely scar revision later.

steps.say: Paediatric repair uses only the child own tissues, because mesh has no place in a growing wall. Repair is always primary repair with fascial closure, and prosthetic patch is never used in children. The defect is closed with strong nonabsorbable suture in layers.
steps.tx: Repair is always **primary repair** (own tissue joining) with **fascial closure** (ring suturing), and **prosthetic patch** (mesh) is never used in children. Growing abdominal walls reject foreign material, so layered suture repair remains the only option. Absorbable sutures are avoided in the fascial layer for strength.

steps.say: No belt, coin or strapping will close the ring, and saying so clearly saves money and worry. Observation needs no truss or strapping, and parental counseling reassures that most defects narrow as the rectus matures. Demonstrating the reducible bulge is calming anxious parents.
steps.tx: **Observation** (watchful waiting) needs no truss or strapping, and **parental counseling** (reassuring explanation) teaches that most defects narrow as the **rectus maturation** (muscle strengthening) progresses. Review yearly with ring measurement until closure or the fifth birthday. Siblings need checking since hernias cluster mildly in families.

steps.say: Rare exceptions break the waiting rule and need the operation within days. Defects with incarceration, skin ulceration or evisceration break the elective rule and need emergency repair with prompt surgery. A painful irreducible bulge with vomiting is never left overnight.
steps.tx: Defects with incarceration, **skin ulceration** (sore breakdown) or **evisceration** (bowel out through skin) break the elective rule and need **emergency repair** (urgent operation). Pain with vomiting or discolouration triggers immediate referral to the surgical team. Cover the defect with moist gauze while resuscitation runs.

steps.say: Two newborn wall defects look similar but behave oppositely, and mixing them up is dangerous. Umbilical hernias differ from omphalocele by skin cover and small umbilical ring, and the two must never be confused in notes or consent. Differential diagnosis is protecting both the plan and the paperwork.
steps.tx: Umbilical hernias differ from **omphalocele** (covered major wall defect) by skin cover and small **umbilical ring** (tiny opening), and the two must never be confused in notes or consent. **Differential diagnosis** (telling the two apart) keeps surgery and counselling correct.
